noodle-shop.title: Noodle Shop
noodle-shop.subtitle: Order a bowl of noodles just how you like it.
noodle-shop.culture: Noodle shops in China are cheap and fast, often costing under 20 yuan. Say 微辣 (mild spicy) to start, but in Sichuan-style shops even mild can be quite hot by foreign standards. You usually pay when you order.

dialogue.en: Hello, I would like a bowl of beef noodles.

pay-bill.title: Paying the Bill
pay-bill.subtitle: Ask for the check and split the cost.
pay-bill.culture: Saying 买单 (mǎi dān) is the common way to ask for the bill. WeChat Pay and Alipay are widely accepted, splitting bills (AA) is common among young people, and tipping is not expected.

dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, mǎi dān.
dialogue.en: Hello, can I get the check?

dialogue.speaker: waiter

dialogue.en: The total is eighty-two yuan.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ men fēn kāi fù.
dialogue.en: We'll pay separately.

dialogue.speaker: waiter
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, wǒ bāng nǐ men fēn kāi suàn.
dialogue.en: Sure, I'll split the bill for you.

milk-tea.title: Milk Tea Shop
milk-tea.subtitle: Choose your sugar level and ice amount.
milk-tea.culture: Chinese milk tea shops let you pick sugar level (full / half / quarter / none) and ice amount (regular / less / no ice). 半糖少冰 is a very popular order. For here you drink in; to go they hand you a bag.

dialogue.text: 你好，我要一杯珍珠奶茶。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ yào yī bēi zhēn zhū nǎi chá.
dialogue.en: Hello, I would like a bubble tea with tapioca pearls.

coffee.title: Coffee Shop
coffee.subtitle: Order a coffee hot or iced.
coffee.culture: Chain shops like Luckin and Starbucks are everywhere in Chinese cities. 美式 means an Americano; always say 热 (hot) or 冰 (iced). Prices range from around 15 to 40 yuan.

dialogue.text: 你好，我要一杯美式咖啡。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒ yào yī bēi měishì kāfēi.
dialogue.en: Hello, I would like a cup of American coffee.

restaurant-order.title: Ordering at a Restaurant
restaurant-order.subtitle: Pick shared dishes and rice for the table.
restaurant-order.culture: At Chinese restaurants dishes are shared in the middle of the table, and each person gets their own bowl of rice. Portions are large — order fewer dishes than people, plus rice.

dialogue.speaker: waiter
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, kěyǐ diǎncài le ma?
dialogue.en: Hello, may we order now?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yī fèn gōngbǎo jīdīng.
dialogue.en: We would like an order of Kung Pao chicken.

takeout-order.title: Ordering Takeout
takeout-order.subtitle: Get food delivered to your door.
takeout-order.culture: Ele.me (饿了么) and Meituan (美团) dominate food delivery in China. A typical delivery takes 30-45 minutes. In the app you can leave notes like 'leave at the door' or 'don't call'.

hotpot.title: Hotpot
hotpot.subtitle: Choose your broth and dipping sauce.
hotpot.culture: A split pot (鸳鸯锅) lets you enjoy mild and spicy broth at once, and dipping sauces are often self-serve. In Chengdu, even 'mild' (微辣) hotpot is still quite spicy by foreign standards.

dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, yào shénme guōdǐ? Yǒu qīngtāng hé málà.
dialogue.en: Hello, what kind of soup base would you like? We have clear broth and spicy.

breakfast-stall.title: Breakfast Stall
breakfast-stall.subtitle: Grab buns and soy milk on the street.
breakfast-stall.culture: Breakfast stalls are cheap and quick — a meal costs around 5-10 yuan. 包子 (steamed buns) and 豆浆 (soy milk) are a classic pair. Many stalls are cash or QR-code only, and seating is limited.

receive-delivery.title: Meeting the Delivery Rider
receive-delivery.subtitle: Answer the rider's call and pick up your food.
receive-delivery.culture: Delivery riders often call when they arrive downstairs. Saying 辛苦了 ('thanks for your hard work') is a polite way to end the chat. Many apartment buildings ask riders to wait at the gate.

dialogue.text: 喂，你的外卖到了，在楼下。
dialogue.pinyin: Wèi, nǐ de wàimài dàole, zài lóuxià.
dialogue.en: Hello, your takeout is here, downstairs.

dialogue.en: Okay, I'll be right down.

reserve-table.title: Booking a Table
reserve-table.subtitle: Reserve by phone for a busy restaurant.
reserve-table.culture: Popular places, especially hotpot, fill up fast on weekends, so booking ahead by phone or app is smart. You usually leave just a surname (姓). Small local eateries are fine for walk-ins.

dialogue.text: 你好，我想订今晚七点的桌子。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐhǎo, wǒ xiǎng dìng jīnwǎn qī diǎn de zhuōzi.
dialogue.en: Hello, I'd like to reserve a table for 7 PM tonight.
